writeup.headline: Devon rates Buy on strong growth and trend, but sits just 3 points above Hold.
writeup.thesis: Devon scores 67, a Buy, and growth does most of the work (score 91). Latest-quarter revenue growth was 73.0% year on year, TTM revenue growth was 16.7%, and growth sped up by 73.9 pp from the previous quarter. Trend is also supportive (75): the price is 1.5% below its 52-week high and the shares are up 45.1% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, though they are 7.3 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. Quality (65) pairs a 23.8% FCF margin with a diluted share count up 47.8% year on year. The balance sheet is the weakest factor (41), with net debt at 2.54 times FCF and cash covering 0.07 of debt. Valuation (60) looks moderate in absolute terms at 2.9x sales and 12.0x FCF, with the FCF yield 3.3 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, but the stock is expensive against its own history.
key_risks: Leverage: net debt is 2.54 times FCF and cash covers only 0.07 of debt.
Share count up 47.8% year on year, which dilutes per-share gains from the jump in revenue.
Expensive against its own history: P/S is more expensive than at 57 of the last 61 month-ends.
Oil and gas price swings could quickly reverse the revenue growth and FCF margin.
Q3 results on November 5 and the $4.2 billion Eagle Ford sale, which still needs regulatory approval, could shift sentiment.
what_would_change: A 3-point drop in the score would move the rating to Hold, for example if growth cools or the trend weakens after Q3 results.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 13 more points, most plausibly from lower leverage lifting the balance sheet score or a cheaper valuation.
Progress on the year-end 2027 synergy target, or a guidance change on November 5, would move the growth and news scores.
